message:
Hotfix: fix syntax error and duplicate wallet-credit in Stripe checkout paths

main was broken -- backend/server.py had a genuine Python SyntaxError
(missing closing parenthesis on an sdb.update_one call) in both
check_payment_status and stripe_webhook, introduced by the merge from
conflict_260726_1352 (PR #2). Confirmed via `python -m py_compile`: the
module could not even be imported, so the backend could not start at
all in this state.

The same edit also reintroduced a bug this project specifically fixed
earlier: an unconditional `wallet_balance += amount` directly on the
users table, running in addition to (not instead of) the existing
atomic, idempotency-guarded ledger credit. Had the syntax error not
existed, this would have double-credited a customer's wallet for a
single payment. Removed both duplicate/malformed update_one calls,
restoring the correct single atomic-transition-then-ledger-credit flow.

Also noted in schema.sql: `paid_at`, written by both of these functions
on the "paid" transition, is not actually a column on the live
payment_transactions table (confirmed against information_schema this
session) -- a separate, pre-existing gap, not something this commit
introduces or fixes on the live database. Documented in schema.sql; not
applied as a migration without confirming first.

Verified: `python -m py_compile backend/server.py` succeeds, and both
existing logic tests (test_ledger_flow.py, test_stripe_collections.py)
still pass.
